transcript:
Header: 2027-07-19 14:00 PDT | Duration: ~75 min | Attendees: Lena Park, Marco Diaz, Tara Singh, Julian Ko, Priya Nair, Samir Patel

Summary section (auto): We ran a wargame for a staged onramp to a new region and a canary model variant. Key risks were quant skew causing kernel fallback, KV-cache warmup impacting latency, and insufficient token cost visibility during surge. Agreed next steps and owners.

[00:00] Lena Park: okay, let's kick off, thanks everyone for carving time for the wargame. we want to run through two scenarios: a slow canary onramp and an accelerated spike with a quant profile change mid-run. keep it rough, this is tabletop plus light sim.
[00:18] Marco Diaz: quick ask — are we using the new q8m quant profile or the legacy q4? that determines fallback surface.
[00:25] Priya Nair: q8m is the target for the canary, but we'll simulate a drift back to q4-stable as a fallback path to see perf regressions.
[00:35] Tara Singh: ok, i'll own oncall play, i'll inject a kernel fallback at T+20 in the accelerated scenario. Julian, you'll emulate infra throttles?
[00:43] Julian Ko: yes I'll throttle the network and bump GPU contention on one slab to see routing decisions.
[00:50] Samir Patel: remember the last release where a small quant skew created 30% latency tail increase, we need to validate KV cache hit ratios as part of this.
[01:02] Lena Park: good call. objective is: no customer-facing latency SLO breaches in the slow canary; in the accelerated case, graceful degradation and clear rollback signal.
[01:12] Marco Diaz: i'll outline the metrics we'll monitor: p50/p95/p99 token latency, kernel-fallback-rate, kv-cache-hit, model-variant-fallback-count, and cost-per-token delta. also trace sampling to link to prompts.
[01:30] Priya Nair: can we add token cost burn-rate as a top-level alert? we had surprise spend last quarter when batching fell apart.
[01:36] Tara Singh: yes, cost burn-rate alert exists but it's aggregated; we need route-level or token-type breakdown. right now console only shows top-level spend by project, not slice.
[01:48] Marco Diaz: that's an observability gap. for the wargame let's assume we have per-route token burn. we'll note the gap as an action item.
[01:55] Lena Park: scenario one — slow canary: 5% of traffic to new region, ramp 1% every 10 minutes over 50 minutes. model: baseline stable q4, canary q8m; autoscale policy: default slab scaling with burst up to 1.5x. aim: confirm latency and cost delta.
[02:15] [00:02:15 - sim start noise] Speaker 1: (sim harness) injecting 1% ramp now
[02:30] Marco Diaz: looking at internal sim dashboard — p50 stable, p95 slight uptick at 20 minutes, kv-cache warming. nothing alarming.
[02:45] Tara Singh: if kv cache is warming we expect tail to normalize by 30-40 minutes if prefix caching warms, but if we see kernel fallback spikes then tail persists.
[03:02] Julian Ko: i see a small number of requests routed to fallback variant due to transient OOM on slot 3 — probably the slab didn't spin up fast enough. that's on the scaling policy config.
[03:18] Priya Nair: can we tighten auto-provision threshold for the canary? i.e., add a secondary proactive spin-up if burst predicted > 25%?
[03:27] Marco Diaz: yes we can add a 2-step threshold: immediate thin spin-up of warm containers plus normal scaling. still, that increases cost. tradeoff discussion...
[03:40] Samir Patel: tradeoff: small incremental cost for protection vs potential SLO violation and bad customer experience, recommend protection for canary.
[03:50] Lena Park: agreed, protect the canary. Marco update action item to tune the policy.
[04:01] [00:04:01] Scenario two — accelerated spike with quant drift: start 20% traffic to new region, at T+12 minutes introduce quant skew on q8m (simulate model param mismatch) and inject a kernel fallback at T+20.
[04:20] Marco Diaz: injecting quant skew now on sim harness...
[04:30] [sim chatter] Speaker 2: logs show kernel selection module flagged an illegal op, falling back to slower kernel route
[04:42] Tara Singh: seeing p99 blow out to ~1.6s, p95 at 700ms; kernel-fallback-rate 8% and climbing. also KV cache hit down 45%.
[04:55] Julian Ko: the routing policy has fallback to cheaper model variant but that variant has different compilation path so we're getting kernel thrash. we should prefer fallback to a compatible quantized variant if available.
[05:10] Marco Diaz: noted — current fallback policy is region-agnostic; we can add model-compatibility as a criteria. that's a config change.
[05:20] Priya Nair: what's the rollback signal? is it kernel-fallback-rate > 5% sustained for two minutes?
[05:28] Tara Singh: our runbook uses sustained token-latency degradation for 3 mins; we should add kernel-fallback metric to the rollback criteria.
[05:36] Samir Patel: also link to cost per token spike; if fallback causes 2x cost and tail latency increase, auto-rollback should trigger.
[05:45] Marco Diaz: one complication: some customers use function-calling patterns that are latency-sensitive but low-volume; they need an exception policy.
[05:53] Lena Park: ok, we'll document an exception list. Priya capture product exceptions.
[06:05] [00:06:05] Crosstalk - Speaker 3: (quiet) what about routing by SLA tier?
[06:12] Marco Diaz: routing by SLA tier exists but not enforced in canary; we should ensure premium traffic never hit canary until it's green. add that to runbook.
[06:22] Lena Park: moving to observability: what traces and logs are missing?
[06:28] Julian Ko: two immediate gaps: per-route token cost and kernel selection trace ids tied to request ids. currently kernel selection logs are in a separate binary and not correlated in tracing.
[06:41] Tara Singh: also health check payloads don't include the compilation profile used; when kernel fallback happens we don't have a quick signal in dashboard to indicate which compile path failed.
[06:52] Marco Diaz: we can add a small telemetry delta: emit compile-profile id and fallback reason as span attributes. low risk change.
[07:02] Priya Nair: timeline to add that to staging? estimate 3 dev days?
[07:08] Marco Diaz: yeah 2-3 days plus one day to surface in the console.
[07:14] Lena Park: add that as an action. Priya will coordinate with Marco.
[07:22] [00:07:22] Breakout: failure injection playbook review.
[07:30] Tara Singh: walk through the inject: kernel-fallback -> route escalation -> cost burn alert -> rollback. if any step fails, oncall escalates to infra and runtime. checklists: toggle canary-off, re-route traffic, scale slab, redeploy compatible variant.
[07:48] Samir Patel: note the redeploy path must have pinned seed for kernel compilers; arbitrary builds cause nondeterministic kernel behavior. we need pinned compile certs in the runbook.
[08:02] Marco Diaz: agreed — pin compiler artifacts per model-variant and record in artifact store.
[08:12] Lena Park: next, communications — who notifies customers? Priya?
[08:18] Priya Nair: product ops will draft a short status note and a longer postmortem template. we should prepare an incident template referencing the rollback thresholds and action owners.
[08:28] [00:08:28] Spike discussion: what if multiple slabs start fallback simultaneously?
[08:35] Julian Ko: then smart routing must divert to other regions or lower tier models; if global capacity constrained, fallback to hosted burst capacity is an option but requires spending approval.
[08:48] Tara Singh: that hosted burst has a slow warmup and is costlier; we shouldn't rely on it except as last resort.
[08:55] Marco Diaz: simulation shows that if two slabs fail, latency tails double and cost triples in worst case, so preemptive rollback is better.
[09:07] Lena Park: conclude with checklist items to update runbook: add kernel-fallback metric to rollback criteria, create per-route token cost alert, pin compiler artifacts, enforce premium routing exclusions for canary, and schedule a dry-run.
[09:25] Priya Nair: i'll consolidate checklist and share by Friday with owners.
[09:33] Marco Diaz: i'll start perf runs tonight and post to #perf tomorrow morning.
[09:40] Tara Singh: i'll set up the failure injection harness and schedule the oncall dry-run for 7/25 maintenance window.
[09:48] Samir Patel: quick risk note — if we tighten automatic rollback triggers too aggressively we might never validate the canary; need balance.
[09:57] Lena Park: totally, use staged alarms: alert, then elevated alert at rollback threshold. manual pause before auto-rollback where appropriate.
[10:10] [00:10:10] Closing recap: owners and due dates.
[10:18] Lena Park: any final questions?
[10:22] Marco Diaz: none.
[10:25] Priya Nair: none, will share doc.
[10:28] Tara Singh: thanks everyone.

End of transcript. Links referenced: runbook draft (link: https://redwood.internal/docs/onramp-runbook), perf dashboard (link: https://grafana.internal/d/serving/perf-sim), sim harness repo (link: https://git.internal/repo/onramp-sim). Note: some names/IDs transcribed imperfectly.
